chunks: From Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Yaqub ibn Shu'ayb who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who emancipated his slave girl and stipulated upon her that she serve him for five years. So she fled, then the man died. His heirs found her. Do they have the right to make her serve them? He said: No.

key_terms.أَبَقَتْ: She fled/ran away; a legal term for a fugitive slave (abq)
key_terms.أَعْتَقَ: Emancipated, freed (a slave); the legal act of granting freedom
key_terms.جَارِيَة: Slave girl; a female slave in classical Islamic jurisprudence
key_terms.شَرَطَ: Stipulated, imposed a condition; a legal term for conditional contracts
key_terms.وَرَثَة: Heirs, inheritors; those who inherit the estate of the deceased

ai.seo_question: Can the heirs of a man who freed his slave girl inherit the right to her service?
ai.summary: Yaqub ibn Shu'ayb posed a legal question to Imam al-Sadiq (AS) about a conditional emancipation: a man freed his slave girl under the condition that she serve him for five years, but she fled before completing the service. When the man died and his heirs found her, the Imam ruled that the heirs have no right to enforce the remaining service obligation. This ruling establishes that conditions attached to emancipation are personal to the original master and do not transfer to his heirs as an inheritable right.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, or said, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from Safwan, from Yaqoub Bin Shuayb who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a man who emancipated his slave girl and stipulated a condition upon her that ‘if she were to serve him for five years’. So she remained, then the man died. So she was found to have inherited him. Is it for them (the family of the deceased) that they make her serve them?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No’.
